profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Capital One
profile.summary:
Software engineer at Capital One and University of Michigan CS alum, building fintech systems from greenfield full-stack platforms to high-volume backend services. I use AI-assisted, spec-driven development to ship fast while keeping code aligned with specs.

My interest in healthcare started as a pharmacy technician, and at Michigan I served as president of MedLaunch, a bio-design engineering organization. I’m looking to bring my engineering experience to fast-paced teams that build with AI, ideally ones using technology for positive impact.

AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Building a greenfield platform that replaces a legacy system used by credit officers to evaluate counterparty risk. Credit officers use it to rate financial institution counterparties, assign credit limits, and monitor the bank’s exposure to each of them. The platform covers 1,000+ financial institutions.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Owned the final delivery and feedback data flows for Capital One’s enterprise messaging platform, which sends email, SMS, push, and paper messages to customers.

positions.title: President
positions.description: I served as President of MedLaunch, an 80+ member student organization at the University of Michigan dedicated to biomedical innovation and entrepreneurship. MedLaunch hosts an annual yearlong Biodesign Challenge, where interdisciplinary teams develop assistive technologies for local community partners. In this role, I led the executive board, oversaw fifteen design projects, coordinated with university leadership and external stakeholders, and organized key events such as design reviews, final showcases, technical workshops, and team-building activities.

volunteerExperiences.description: I help with the venue set-up and tear-down for annual BAPS Charities health fairs at my local BAPS temple in Canton, MI. We aim to bring physicians and other medical professionals to volunteer their expertise and time to provide medical care and advice to people who may lack access to such care. With an emphasis on education and preventative care, these fairs have proved to be invaluable in promoting healthy living and decreasing medical costs.

I raised funds for our annual BAPS Charities Walk Green Walkathons. BAPS Charities is working with The Nature Conservancy’s efforts to plant one billion trees by 2025 through their Plant a Billion Trees initiative. During the last four years, from 2016 to 2019, BAPS Charities Walkathons will have helped plant a total of 361,000 trees.
